input.command: grep -rn "runnable\|createFixTask\|poll\|TaskStore" src package.json; git status --short | head

input.reason: In src/tasks.ts, createFixTask (line 13) builds a local `task` with `state: "running", feedback: null` (line 14), inserts it (line 15), and then writes the feedback to the store in a separate `store.update(id, { feedback })` call (line 16). That update only changes the store. It never changes the local `task` object. So `emit({ ...task })` on line 17 always sends `feedback: null`, and the returned `task` on line 18 also has null feedback. This happens on every call, not only under a race. The poll race is also plausible. The record is stored as `running` with null feedback before line 16 runs, and poll (lines 21-24) runs whatever `store.runnable()` returns. However, no TaskStore implementation exists in the repository, so I can't confirm which states runnable() includes or whether poll can see the gap between the two writes. The emit/return defect alone confirms the issue at the fix location. Nothing in the repo calls createFixTask, and I found no guard that would stop it.
input.failure_scenario: Call createFixTask(store, "t1", "please fix the null check", emit). The store gets {id:"t1", state:"running", feedback:null}, and then its feedback is updated. But emit receives {id:"t1", state:"running", feedback:null}, and the caller gets back a Task whose feedback is also null. Any listener or dashboard that relies on the emitted event never sees the feedback. Also, if a concurrent poll() calls store.runnable() between the insert and the update, and the store treats running tasks as runnable, run() gets the task without its feedback.
input.severity_reason: The emitted event and the returned value lose the feedback on every createFixTask call, not only in a rare race, so the wrong data sits on the main path for creating fix tasks. This is not a security or persistence issue, because the store does end up holding the feedback.
